title: Fraction of vertices with notable neighbors
statement: Let $G$ be a regular unique game with alphabet size $q$, let a long-code table and a real parameter $\\varepsilon$ be given, and choose a vertex uniformly from $G$. The neighbor notable vertex fraction is the probability that the set of notable coordinates at that vertex's neighbors is nonempty.
hypotheses_covered: A regular unique game $G$ with alphabet size $q$
A long-code table on the vertices of $G$
caveat: The supplied statement does not define the neighbor notable-coordinate set or specify the neighbor sampling law beyond the expectation notation.
